rpspanel: US state energy-economy panels with RPS stringency measures

Source: R/rpspanel-package.R
rpspanel-package.Rd

The package has four layers:

Details

  1. Fetch and cache: fetch_eia(), fetch_bea(), fetch_census(), fetch_rps() download each source through its API (or read the bundled RPS coding), cache the result locally and fail with clear messages when a service is unavailable.

  2. Harmonise: harmonise_states(), deflate(), convert_units() align state codes, units and price bases.

  3. Panel builder: build_panel() merges everything into one tidy state-year table with source and vintage attributes.

  4. RPS stringency: rps_rules() and rps_stringency() turn coded RPS rules into annual stringency indices.

Documentation helpers (codebook(), cite_sources()) and output helpers (as_pdata(), export_panel()) complete the workflow.

API keys

EIA and BEA data require free API keys. Store them in your .Renviron file as EIA_API_KEY and BEA_API_KEY, plus CENSUS_API_KEY if you use fetch_census().

Options

  • rpspanel.cache_dir: directory used for the download cache (default tools::R_user_dir("rpspanel", "cache")).

  • rpspanel.cache_max_age: maximum age of cached downloads in days (default Inf, so data vintages stay pinned until you refresh them).
